locations.name: Plage de Bon-Secours (tidal pool)
locations.notes: Official 4-year classification 2022–2025 is Insufficient (G→S→I→I). The site is open and the ARS reports no poor in-season results in 2026 to date, but it remains under active remediation; treat as a water-quality advisory and heed on-site flags. The unique seawater tidal pool with a diving tower, sheltered inside the city walls, is the family highlight.

temperatureShelter.rationale: Seawater tidal pool set against the city walls offers a sheltered, swimmable basin regardless of tide state, unlike the exposed Sillon beach.

tides.rationale: The tidal pool holds water through the tidal cycle, so swimming is available even at low tide — the main reason it beats the open Sillon beach for families.

easyAccess.rationale: Walkable from inside walled Saint-Malo; no car needed and direct from the old town.

lifeguards.rationale: Monitored during the summer season with a first-aid post; verify daily coverage on site.

waterQuality.rationale: Official 2025 classification Insufficient (under remediation). Still open and compliant in-season 2026, but flagged — see the advisory warning above.

alternatives.rationale: Saint-Malo has 14 monitored bathing sites nearby (Sillon, Rochebonne, Bas Sablons) plus Cancale beaches a short drive away, giving many fallbacks.

locations.name: Lac de Trémelin
locations.officialSource: ARS Bretagne / baignades.sante.gouv.fr — Lac de Trémelin (Iffendic, 35)
locations.notes: Official 4-year classification 2022–2025 is Excellent throughout. Blue Flag, lifeguarded 13:30–19:00 late June to end of August; ARS water sampling runs all season. A freshwater inland counterpoint to the Morbihan coast on the Brocéliande axis.

temperatureShelter.rationale: Forest-fringed freshwater lake in the Brocéliande area; water reaches ~20 °C in summer and the forest gives wind shelter, warmer and calmer than the open coast.

tides.rationale: A lake has no tidal cycle, so water level and swimmability are stable all day — no tide-table dependency at all.

easyAccess.rationale: Equipped beach with pontoon and facilities, but it is an inland site reached by car from the Vannes/Carnac base (~1 h drive).

lifeguards.rationale: Lifeguarded every afternoon in season (late June–end August); swimming is only permitted during supervised hours.

waterQuality.rationale: Official 4-year classification Excellent (E every year 2022–2025); Blue Flag awarded since 2017.

alternatives.rationale: A single inland lake rather than a cluster; the on-site leisure base (tree-top trail, sailing, riding) broadens the day but other swimming spots need a drive.

locations.name: Lac de Guerlédan
locations.officialSource: ARS Bretagne / baignades.sante.gouv.fr — Anse de Guerlédan (Guerlédan, 22)
locations.notes: Official 4-year classification 2022–2025 is Excellent (two monitored inlets, Anse de Guerlédan and Anse de Landroannec, both E every year). Brittany's largest freshwater lake, sitting between the Quimper/South-Finistère and Côte-de-Granit-Rose areas; no corpus coverage so provenance here is official-source only.

temperatureShelter.rationale: Large sheltered inland freshwater lake — warmer in summer than the Atlantic and protected from coastal wind.

tides.rationale: Freshwater lake with no tidal cycle; swimmable throughout the day.

easyAccess.rationale: Equipped beaches (Plage de Beau Rivage area) but inland, a longer drive from the Quimper base; best paired with a Côte-de-Granit-Rose stay.

lifeguards.rationale: Designated, supervised swimming zones operate in the summer season; swim only within the marked areas.

waterQuality.rationale: Official 4-year classification Excellent (E every year 2022–2025 at both monitored inlets).

alternatives.rationale: Multiple coves and water-sport hire around the lake give variety within one destination, though other monitored beaches are a drive away.

locations.name: Lac au Duc
locations.officialSource: ARS Bretagne / baignades.sante.gouv.fr — Lac au Duc (Taupont, 56)
locations.notes: Official 4-year classification 2022–2025 is Excellent throughout. A freshwater lake near Ploërmel on the Morbihan inland axis; no corpus coverage, so provenance is official-source only. Seasonal sampling showed occasional 'Moyen' (average) readings late August 2024, all within compliance and the overall grade stayed Excellent.

temperatureShelter.rationale: Sheltered inland freshwater lake; warmer than the Atlantic in summer and set back from the windy coast.

tides.rationale: Freshwater lake with no tidal cycle; stable water level all day.

easyAccess.rationale: Equipped beach and leisure facilities near Ploërmel, reachable by car from the Vannes/Carnac base in under an hour.

lifeguards.rationale: Supervised swimming zone operates during the summer season; swim within marked areas.

waterQuality.rationale: Official 4-year classification Excellent (E every year 2022–2025), monitored all season for microbiology and cyanobacteria.

alternatives.rationale: A single lake with a leisure base (sailing, walking) rather than a cluster of swimming spots.

locations.name: Plage de Morgat
locations.officialSource: ARS Bretagne / baignades.sante.gouv.fr — Morgat (Le Loc'h & Toul an Trez), Crozon (29)
locations.notes: Official 4-year classification 2022–2025 Excellent at both monitored Morgat points (Le Loc'h and Toul an Trez). An enclosed bay on the Crozon peninsula described as the area's most sheltered family swimming spot, with kayak and paddleboard hire.

temperatureShelter.rationale: Enclosed bay shelters the beach from open-ocean swell; sea water stays ~18 °C in August (refreshing, not warm) but the bay is calmer than the exposed Crozon headlands.

tides.rationale: An enclosed bay holds a gentler tidal range than the exposed Crozon points; still check tide times, but swimming is practical across more of the day.

easyAccess.rationale: Town beach in Morgat with direct access and water-sport hire; a car is effectively essential to reach the Crozon peninsula, however.

lifeguards.rationale: Monitored bathing site during the summer season; follow on-site flags.

waterQuality.rationale: Official 4-year classification Excellent at both monitored points (Le Loc'h E in 2025 after a B in 2024; Toul an Trez E every year).

alternatives.rationale: The Crozon peninsula clusters several monitored beaches (Aber, Kersiguenou, Kador) plus the Île Vierge viewpoint, giving real variety within a short drive.

locations.name: Grande Plage de Carnac
locations.officialSource: ARS Bretagne / baignades.sante.gouv.fr — Carnac Grande Plage (56)
locations.notes: Official 4-year classification 2022–2025 Excellent. Blue Flag family beach ~2 km long, sheltered by the Quiberon peninsula from heavy swell, with lifeguards and beach clubs running in August; the warmest and calmest bathing water in the shortlist.

temperatureShelter.rationale: The Morbihan south coast is the warmest part of the shortlist — sea water reaches ~19 °C in August — and the Quiberon peninsula shelters the beach from open swell.

tides.rationale: A gentle slope and sheltered aspect mean the beach stays usable across the tidal range, with calmer water than the north or west coasts.

easyAccess.rationale: A resort beach with direct town access, beach clubs, facilities and a gentle slope — purpose-built for families.

lifeguards.rationale: Lifeguarded with beach clubs running through August.

waterQuality.rationale: Official 4-year classification Excellent (E every year 2022–2025); Blue Flag.

alternatives.rationale: Carnac has several Blue Flag beaches (Grande Plage, Saint-Colomban) and the Quiberon peninsula's beaches and ferries are close by.
